candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Find a common denominator and rewrite one or more fractional parts as equivalent fractions with matching denominators before subtraction.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: B.S01 and C.S01 match directly in name, scope, and exclusions. A does include common-denominator work inside S01, but A.S01 is broader because it also includes rewriting whole numbers and normalizing mixed numbers, so A.S01 is aligned to a broader operand-rewriting concept instead of this narrower denominator-only concept.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Rewrite a whole number or mixed number into a subtraction-ready form, such as adding a zero-fraction part, expressing a whole as whole plus fractional units, or normalizing a nonstandard mixed number.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A.S01 and C.S02 both cover preparatory rewriting beyond denominator alignment, including adding fractional parts to whole numbers and normalizing improper mixed numbers. B has no separate skill for this because B.S03 combines normalization with borrowing/regrouping, so no B skill is equivalent at this granularity.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Subtract fractions with a shared denominator and/or subtract whole-number and fractional parts separately once the quantities are in compatible form.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: All three experts define the same core computation step: perform subtraction after alignment or rewriting is complete, excluding denominator creation, regrouping, and final simplification.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Regroup one whole into fractional units so subtraction can continue when the fractional part of the minuend is too small.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A.S03 isolates borrowing/regrouping as its own skill. B and C do include borrowing, but only inside broader combined skills that also include other operations, so there is no directly equivalent standalone skill in those codebooks.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Rewrite a quantity either by normalizing a nonstandard mixed number or by regrouping one whole into fractional units so subtraction can proceed correctly.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: B.S03 uniquely combines two ideas that other experts separate: normalization of improper mixed numbers and borrowing/regrouping. A splits these across A.S01 and A.S03, while C splits them across C.S02 and C.S04, so B.S03 stands as a broader composite concept without a single equivalent elsewhere.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Reduce a subtraction result to lowest terms and express it in an appropriate final form such as a fraction, mixed number, whole number, or zero.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A.S04 and B.S04 align closely as final-result processing skills focused on simplification and final expression. C does include simplification, but only bundled together with regrouping in C.S04, so C has no standalone equivalent at this level.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Borrow one whole into fractional units when needed and then express the result in lowest terms or final integer/mixed-number form.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: C.S04 uniquely combines borrowing/regrouping with final simplification and expression. A and B separate or differently bundle these operations, so no single A or B skill is equivalent to this exact composite concept.

alignment_summary: The three codebooks share strong consensus on the core subtraction operation and partial consensus on preparation and finalization steps, but they differ substantially in granularity. A separates preparation, subtraction, borrowing, and simplification; B separates common denominators and subtraction but combines normalization with regrouping; C separates denominator creation and operand rewriting but combines regrouping with simplification. Every expert skill_id was mapped exactly once, with several 1/3 concepts arising from these different bundling choices rather than from wholly unrelated content.
